questions.stem: Which of the following defines Direction of Arrival (DOA)?
questions.key: The azimuthal angle indicating the direction from which the RF signal is arriving relative to the RDF system
distractors: The difference in arrival times of an RF signal at multiple spatially separated antennas
The phase difference between signals received at two or more separate antennas
The distance from the RDF system to the RF source along the signal path
questions.explanation: DOA is defined as the azimuthal angle indicating the direction from which the RF signal arrives relative to the RDF system.
why: That is the quantity compared in the TDOA method, not the DOA itself.
That is the quantity compared in phase comparison, a method used to find the DOA.
DOA is an angle, not a distance.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes Phase Comparison (Differential RDF)?
questions.key: It compares the phase of the signal received at two or more separate antennas to determine the direction of the RF source
distractors: It uses the difference in arrival times of the RF signal at multiple spatially separated antennas
It combines bearings from several sites to fix the position of the source
It integrates directional information into command and control systems
questions.explanation: Phase comparison measures the phase difference between signals at different antennas and uses it to determine the direction of the RF source.
why: That is Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA).
Triangulation is a training concept, not the phase comparison method.
Integration with command and control is an RDF concept, not a measurement method.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA)?
questions.key: It uses the difference in arrival times of the RF signal at multiple spatially separated antennas
distractors: It compares the phase of the signal received at two or more separate antennas
It reads the azimuthal angle from which the signal arrives relative to the RDF system
It locates distress beacons used by aircraft, ships and individuals
questions.explanation: TDOA methods use the differences in the times the RF signal reaches multiple spatially separated antennas.
why: That is Phase Comparison.
That is the definition of DOA, the result, not the TDOA method.
That is a role of RDF (emergency beacons), not a measurement method.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the civilian applications of RDFs?
questions.key: Spectrum monitoring, identifying sources of interference, and locating emergency distress signals
distractors: Locating enemy communication centers, radar installations and other electronic emissions
Intercepting tactical radios, satellite communications and radar signals for reconnaissance
Determining the direction of radio beacons to aid marine and aviation navigation only
questions.explanation: Civilian applications are spectrum monitoring, identifying sources of interference and locating emergency distress signals from aircraft, ships or beacons.
why: That is the military application.
That is the military communications source category.
Navigation is a separate role, and the word 'only' leaves out the other civilian uses.

questions.stem: It is the method in which RDF systems use the phase differences of signals received at different antenna pairs or elements to determine the DOA.
questions.explanation: Interferometric RDF compares phase differences between antenna pairs or elements to accurately determine the azimuth of the RF source.
why: TDOA compares arrival times, not phase differences.
Triangulation is mentioned as a training concept, not as an interferometric method.
DOA is the result being measured, not a method.

questions.stem: It is the RDF role in which signals are located to guide responders to survivors or downed aircraft in remote or inaccessible areas.
questions.explanation: Slide 15: in search and rescue, RDFs pinpoint distress signals to guide responders to survivors or downed aircraft in remote or inaccessible areas.
why: Navigation and Positioning uses the direction of radio beacons to establish position.
Monitoring and Surveillance covers border security, law enforcement and spectrum enforcement.
Border Surveillance detects unauthorized signals near the borders.

questions.stem: It is the RDF role historically used in marine and aviation to determine the direction of radio beacons without relying on visual landmarks or GPS.
questions.explanation: Navigation and Positioning helps establish position from the direction of radio beacons or signals.
why: Search and Rescue pinpoints distress signals.
Monitoring and Surveillance deals with unauthorized transmissions and regulations.
Locating RF Sources covers finding military and civilian emitters.

questions.stem: A government agency uses RDF to detect unauthorized transmissions and enforce radio spectrum regulations. Which role of RDFs is this?
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Surveillance covers border security, law enforcement and intelligence use, including detecting unauthorized transmissions and enforcing spectrum regulations.
why: Navigation and Positioning concerns direction to radio beacons.
Search and Rescue concerns distress signals.
Training and Capability Development concerns maintaining proficiency in RDF operations.

questions.stem: A radar installation emits distinctive RF signals, and the Army uses RDF to locate it and identify enemy radar sites. Which category of RF source is this?
questions.explanation: Radar installations emit distinctive RF signals that RDFs can detect and locate to identify enemy radar sites.
why: Military communications are tactical radios and satellite communications.
Civilian communications are broadcast stations and cellular networks.
Emergency beacons are distress transmitters used by aircraft, ships and individuals.

questions.stem: Army personnel use RDF to detect and locate radio signals coming from unauthorized or suspicious sources near the country's borders. Which RDF concept does this describe?
questions.explanation: Border Surveillance uses RDF to detect and locate signals from unauthorized or suspicious sources near borders.
why: Communication Monitoring analyzes transmissions within the operational area and secures military communications.
Intelligence Gathering intercepts and locates enemy communication signals.
Search and Rescue locates distress signals from downed aircraft or stranded personnel.

questions.stem: A signal officer explains that RDF information is fed into the Army's broader systems so operations can be coordinated and resources managed from real-time intelligence. Which RDF concept is this?
questions.key: Integration with Command and Control Systems
questions.explanation: RDF is integrated into command and control systems to coordinate operations, manage resources and respond rapidly based on real-time intelligence.
why: Communication Monitoring detects and analyzes transmissions in the operational area.
Training and Capability Development maintains proficiency in RDF principles and equipment.
Intelligence Gathering intercepts and locates enemy signals about movements and intentions.

questions.stem: Which list contains the three methods used in RDF to determine direction of arrival (DOA)?
questions.key: Phase comparison, Time Difference of Arrival, Interferometric techniques
distractors: Phase comparison, Time Difference of Arrival, Signal triangulation
Time Difference of Arrival, Interferometric techniques, Spectrum monitoring
Phase comparison, Interferometric techniques, Bearing processing
questions.explanation: The lesson names Phase Comparison, Time Difference of Arrival and Interferometric Techniques as DOA methods.
why: Triangulation is a training concept, not a DOA method.
Spectrum monitoring is an application, not a method.
Bearing processing is not one of the named methods; TDOA is missing.

questions.stem: Which list contains the four RDF roles taught in the lesson?
questions.key: Locating RF Sources, Navigation and Positioning, Search and Rescue, Monitoring and Surveillance
distractors: Locating RF Sources, Navigation and Positioning, Search and Rescue, Border Surveillance
Locating RF Sources, Navigation and Positioning, Training, Monitoring and Surveillance
Locating RF Sources, Communication Monitoring, Search and Rescue, Monitoring and Surveillance
questions.explanation: The roles are Locating RF Sources, Navigation and Positioning, Search and Rescue, and Monitoring and Surveillance.
why: Border Surveillance is an RDF concept, not one of the four roles.
Training is an RDF concept, and Search and Rescue is missing.
Communication Monitoring is an RDF concept, and Navigation and Positioning is missing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a category of RF source named in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Slides 17-20 name military communications, radar systems, civilian communications and emergency beacons as RF sources. TDOA is a method for determining direction of arrival (slide 28), not an RF source.
why: Military communications is a named RF source (slide 17).
Radar systems is a named RF source (slide 18).
Emergency beacons is a named RF source (slide 20).
